articles.title: Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59
articles.summary: Indian filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, whose credits include the crime thriller “Kaante,” the gangster saga “Shootout at Wadala” and the Hrithik Roshan-starring “Kaabil,” has died following a fall at his Mumbai residence on Oct. 30. He was 59, according to the Press Trust of India.
body: Police in Mumbai’s Versova neighborhood have filed an accidental death report. Deputy Commissioner of Police Purushottam Karad told the Free Press Journal that members of Gupta’s family were sleeping when the incident occurred and became aware of it the following morning. “The family has not raised any suspicion or lodged a complaint,” Karad said.

Gupta was a prominent exponent of the glossy, action-driven Hindi-language crime thriller, bringing a visual sensibility heavily indebted to Hollywood to an industry traditionally dominated by melodrama and musicals. His career behind the camera began with “Aatish: Feel the Fire” in 1994, featuring Sanjay Dutt and Aditya Pancholi. He subsequently directed “Ram Shastra,” “Jung” and “Khauff,” developing an enduring professional relationship with Dutt that extended across 10 films, including projects Gupta produced.

articles.title: Pink Film Veteran Zeze Takahisa Champions Original Stories at Tokyo Masterclass
articles.summary: The Tokyo International Film Festival’s Tokyo Talk program presented a masterclass with Zeze Takahisa, director of the festival’s opening film, “Sukiyaki.” Held before a full-house crowd at Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, the talk focused on Zeze’s early “pink” (softcore porn) and indie films, followed by…
body: The Tokyo International Film Festival ’s Tokyo Talk program presented a masterclass with Zeze Takahisa, director of the festival’s opening film, “Sukiyaki.”

Pink films screened in specialized theaters for an exclusively male audience, and directors had to insert a bed scene every 10 minutes or so. “I’ve always been pretty firm in my convictions,” said Zeze. “Starting from the early 1990s the culture shifted and I had more freedom to say what I wanted. That kind of thing was important to me.”
At the time, Zeze was interested in stories about female criminals. “It’s just different from the male perspective,” he said. “The motives behind the crimes and so on. I found it fascinating.”

Scripted by Zeze, “Extracurricular Activity: Rape” was about delinquent high school girls who hang out at Tokyo’s Haneda Airport and battle the yakuza. Zeze gave it the “private” title “Go to Haneda and You Will See Kids Dressed Like Pirates Ready to Attack.”

articles.title: Japan’s Film Funds Look Beyond Production Committees to Build New Financing Models
articles.summary: Japan’s production committee system, in which a group of companies jointly finance a film and share its rights, has helped spread risk across the industry. But it can also cap budgets at what the industry itself can raise, make it harder for overseas investors to take part and slow decisions when…
body: “Film Funds in Japan: What Works, What Doesn’t, and What Comes Next” featured Kii Muneyuki, CEO and producer of K2 Pictures, which works with filmmakers including Kore-eda Hirokazu, Miike Takashi and Nishikawa Miwa; Ibe Tomonobu, CEO of Questry, a Tokyo startup that uses digital securities to fund anime and other Japanese content; Nakagawa Keita, managing director at MUFG Bank; and Motoyanagi Yusuke, partner at law firm Nishimura & Asahi.

Kii presented K2P Film Fund I as one example of a new structure. The fund closed in February at about JPY5 billion ($32 million) and aims to back around 50 films over seven years. It is a blind pool, meaning investors commit money before the films are chosen. Its investors include MUFG, the Development Bank of Japan and other financial institutions and companies, and a greenlight committee oversees project approvals. Kii said five films had been released in theaters in 2026.
points: Japan’s production committee system, in which a group of companies jointly finance a film and share its rights, has helped spread risk across the industry.

articles.title: Japan’s New 2027 Anime Award Should Put Creators in the Spotlight, Industry Leaders Say at Tokyo Market
articles.summary: A new Japanese anime award planned for 2027 should put the people who make anime in the spotlight, industry leaders said at TIFFCOM, the market of the Tokyo International Film Festival. The session was moderated by Fujitsu Ryota, programming advisor for the festival’s animation section.
body: The award’s name and outline will be revealed Nov. 2 at the closing event of Tokyo Anime Next, the festival that organized the session. Co-hosted by the AJA and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Tokyo Anime Next runs Oct. 30–Nov. 2 in Tokyo’s Ikebukuro district, with several events at TIFFCOM.
The 2027 launch date has yet to be confirmed, and the panelists stressed that their views were not the award’s official positions.
“Creators should be highlighted – and they should be put in the limelight,” Shimizu said when asked about the timing of the launch.

Saito Masaya said Toho had helped work on the concept for the award, and agreed that creators should be highlighted. He added that the award could give fans a more direct connection to the people behind anime’s global popularity. The company wants to “help achieve a wider reach to anime fans and help give them a wider perspective,” he said, bringing them closer to different creative styles and approaches.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors comes to a climax in nail-biting final
articles.summary: The second series of the hit show reached its climax on Friday after attracting 15 million viewers.
body: We've had four weeks of suspense, suspicion and very suspect tactics, as some of Britain's biggest stars engaged in a battle of wits to win the most popular show on TV.
The second series of BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors reached its climax on Friday, with the 21 original contestants having been reduced to seven before the final.
They were then whittled down to two winners - with the faithful duo of comedian Romesh Ranganathan and Heartstopper actor Sebastian "Bash" Croft emerging victorious.
The players successfully banished the remaining traitors - Love Island host Maya Jama and YouTuber King Kenny - in dramatic fashion, and the winning pair shared the £83,000 prize for their charities.

articles.title: Rob Zombie's Disturbing Horror Movie Trilogy Is Worth Revisiting For Halloween
articles.summary: Rob Zombie's controversial, ultra-violent cult favorite horror trilogy now has a new 4K box set just in time for Halloween.
body: I have a bit of a love/hate relationship with the films of Rob Zombie. I think Mr. Zombie has great instincts as a director and is able to create effective, disturbing images. On the other hand, he's a dreadful screenwriter, especially when it comes to dialogue — he's fond of having his characters utter non-stop obscenities that make them sound like grade schoolers who just discovered curse words exist. And yet, Zombie is clearly such a horror nerd — the type who would likely be haunting horror conventions looking for autographs if he wasn't a rich and famous guy — that I can't help but appreciate him.

Zombie made the leap to filmmaking with "House of 1000 Corpses," a silly, nasty piece of work that inadvertently launched an entire trilogy of films. That trilogy, dubbed Rob Zombie's Firefly Trilogy, now has a nifty new 4K box set from Lionsgate, just in time for Halloween. Zombie clearly loves Halloween season as much as he loves horror movies, and that's another thing that endears him to me: I'm a big old Halloween nerd.

articles.title: How Bristol shaped Maya Jama before her TV fame
articles.summary: The Love Island host's journey from leaving Bristol as a teenager to reaching the BBC show's finale.
body: Maya Jama has gone from Bristol schoolgirl to one of the UK's biggest television stars.
The 32-year-old Love Island host was watched by millions as she faced the last round table in the final of The Celebrity Traitors, which aired on BBC One and iPlayer.
But behind the glamorous television appearances and red carpet moments is a story that began in a council house with a young girl determined to make it on the small screen.
Maya was born and raised in Bristol, growing up in St Paul's with a family of Bristol Rovers supporters, putting on song and dance performances for them and charging 20p a time.

articles.title: Party Rock Anthem singer struggled with mental health before death
articles.summary: Lauren Bennett, who featured on LMFAO's hit song, was found dead by her husband.
body: A British singer who was a member of the girl group G.R.L took her own life, an inquest has found.
Lauren Bennett, 36, who also featured on LMFAO's 2011 hit Party Rock Anthem, was found dead in Kent on 29 May.
In a statement read out by an assistant coroner on Friday, her husband Kenny Wormald said she had been struggling with severe mental health issues before her death.
The court heard she told him she was going out for a walk on the morning of her death while he remained in bed half asleep.

articles.title: The MCU's Best Action Thriller Is the Perfect James Bond Replacement
articles.summary: Nearly 20 years after Iron Man rocketed into theaters, the Marvel Cinematic Universe continues to flourish. Part of that is because the franchise is a constant; despite its ups and downs, people expected at least one Marvel movie in theaters each year.
body: We're talking, of course, about Captain America: The Winter Soldier. Directed by Joe and Anthony Russo, The Winter Soldier sees Steve Rogers ( Chris Evans ) working with S.H.I.E.L.D. to neutralize terrorist threats. When S.H.I.E.L.D. director Nick Fury ( Samuel L. Jackson ) is seemingly assassinated, Steve comes face to face with the shadowy figure known as the 'Winter Soldier'— and a conspiracy that forces him and Natasha Romanoff ( Scarlett Johansson ) to go on the run. Captain America: The Winter Soldier stands above other MCU movies due to its grittier tone, and it helped set the stage for the franchise's future.

"We wanted it to be Cap versus the world we all live in today. He'd just fought aliens, and it didn't seem like the time to double down and have him up against dinosaurs and magicians. He's a man named after a country, and eventually, you've got to check in on the state of the country."

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart remembered as 'Mirfield's finest'
articles.summary: Tributes have been paid to the legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart, who was born in Mirfield.
body: Sir Patrick Stewart once said he had to drop his Yorkshire accent for Hollywood, but he never forgot his roots.

The Mirfield-born actor, best known for his roles in Star Trek and the X-Men films, died at the age of 86 at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday after suffering with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
His death has prompted an outpouring of love from the community he proudly called home, along with his beloved Huddersfield Town - the club he followed from childhood.
Stewart's friend and fellow legendary actor Sir Ian McKellen said Stewart "never forsook his origins".

articles.title: 13 Years Later, Michael B. Jordan's Career-Best Performance Is Officially Free to Stream
articles.summary: As the race for next year's Academy Awards gains momentum, there's one film that is the favorite to sweep up. Christopher Nolan 's historical epic The Odyssey, which stars Matt Damon as the King of Ithaca, is likely to take home several Golden Statues come the 99th Oscars ceremony.
body: Of its 16 nominations, Sinners took home four trophies, including the awards for Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score. But its most notable win came in the Best Actor category, as Michael B. Jordan somewhat surprised cinephiles by beating Timothée Chalamet to the prize. There's no doubt that Jordan deserved the win, with his dual performance as both of the Smokestack Twins his best yet. But all of Jordan's best work has come under the directorial eye of Coogler, with their first collaboration being the film that put both men on the map.

After debuting at the 2013 Sundance Film Festival to widespread critical acclaim, earning the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in the process, the brilliant drama Fruitvale Station caught the attention of Hollywood, with Coogler and Jordan being fast-tracked to the top. In Collider's review at the time, Matt Goldberg awarded a "B+" score, one of countless gushing responses to the film. If you're a fan of either star but have yet to see their most important and influential movie, you're in luck, as Fruitvale Station will be available to stream for free on Plex, starting November 1.
